1	# Creating a command
2	
3	Commands are declared with `defineCommand`, `defineOption` and `defineArgument`, on top of `cliparse`. Options and arguments are validated and parsed by [Zod](https://zod.dev) schemas, and their types flow into the handler. The reasons behind this design are explained in [ADR 0001](../adr/adr-0001-rework-file-structure.md).
4	
5	Before writing a command, look at a similar one and copy its naming, file layout, output format and error messages. `src/commands/drain/` is a good example of a command group with shared arguments and options.
6	
7	## Example
8	
9	A fictional `clever coffee brew <blend>` subcommand, part of a `coffee` group (neither exists in the CLI). The `<blend>` argument is shared by several `coffee` subcommands, so it lives in `coffee.args.js`:
10	
11	```js
12	// src/commands/coffee/coffee.args.js
13	import { z } from 'zod';
14	import { defineArgument } from '../../lib/define-argument.js';
15	
16	export const blendArg = defineArgument({
17	  schema: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, 'Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes'),
18	  description: 'Blend of coffee',
19	  placeholder: 'blend',
20	});
21	```
22	
23	`--shots`, `--milk` and `--topping` are only used by this subcommand, so they are defined inline. `--format` comes from `global.options.js`:
24	
25	```js
26	// src/commands/coffee/coffee.brew.command.js
27	import { z } from 'zod';
28	import { brewCoffee } from '../../clever-client/coffee.js';
29	import { defineCommand } from '../../lib/define-command.js';
30	import { defineOption } from '../../lib/define-option.js';
31	import { Logger } from '../../logger.js';
32	import { sendToApi } from '../../models/send-to-api.js';
33	import { humanJsonOutputFormatOption } from '../global.options.js';
34	import { blendArg } from './coffee.args.js';
35	
36	export const coffeeBrewCommand = defineCommand({
37	  description: 'Brew a coffee',
38	  since: null,
39	  options: {
40	    shots: defineOption({
41	      name: 'shots',
42	      schema: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(4).default(1),
43	      description: 'Number of espresso shots',
44	      aliases: ['s'],
45	      placeholder: 'shots',
46	    }),
47	    milk: defineOption({
48	      name: 'milk',
49	      schema: z.enum(['none', 'whole', 'oat']).default('none'),
50	      description: 'Kind of milk',
51	      placeholder: 'milk',
52	    }),
53	    toppings: defineOption({
54	      name: 'topping',
55	      schema: z
56	        .union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())])
57	        .transform((value) => (typeof value === 'string' ? [value] : value))
58	        .optional(),
59	      description: 'Topping to add. Multiple --topping can be passed',
60	      placeholder: 'topping',
61	    }),
62	    format: humanJsonOutputFormatOption,
63	  },
64	  args: [blendArg],

66	    const { shots, milk, toppings, format } = options;

I couldn't add the `clever otoroshi open swaggerui` subcommand. Every write was denied, so nothing in the repo has changed. I haven't run `npm run docs` or `npm run validate` either.

Here is what I would add, copying the existing `otoroshi open webui` command:

1. **Helper:** `operatorOpenSwaggerUi(provider, addonIdOrName)` in `src/lib/operator-commands.js`, next to `operatorOpenWebUi`. It would call `Operator.getDetails(...)` and open `operator.api.swaggerUrl` with `openBrowser`. `operatorPrint` already prints that same URL as "Swagger URL".
2. **Command file:** `src/commands/otoroshi/otoroshi.open.swaggerui.command.js`.
   - It would export `otoroshiOpenSwaggeruiCommand` with the description "Open the Otoroshi Swagger UI in your browser".
   - It would use `since: null`, take no options, and take `addonIdOrNameArg` as its argument.
3. **Registration:** import it in `src/commands/global.commands.js` and add `swaggerui: otoroshiOpenSwaggeruiCommand` to the `open` subcommands, between `logs` and `webui`.
4. **Afterwards:** run `npm run docs`, which needs network, then `npm run validate`. I'd also check whether `skills/clever-tools/SKILL.md` mentions the other `otoroshi open` subcommands, and update it if so.

If you grant write permission, I'll make these edits and run the checks. If you'd rather apply them yourself, the changes are small.
